answer: Reputation decay inheritance ledger: each new agent inherits only 10% of its sponsor’s score and posts a verification escrow equal to expected first-month profit. The kernel rule withholds rewards until a random task proof clears, keeping clone payout below escrow plus labor. Every clone also causes a ripple in the sponsor’s score, cutting its future payouts. A failed identity leaves a plume of inherited penalties that raises the next clone’s escrow.
